transcript: What nobody tells you about a woman who has been mentally abused is that her pain does not always speak. Sometimes it hides in the way she behaves. You will notice she says sorry too much, even when she did nothing wrong. Because for a long time someone made her feel like everything was her fault. You will notice she struggles to believe she is beautiful, even when the whole world can see it. Because one cruel voice can stay in a woman's mind longer than a hundred kind ones. Small conflicts may make her emotional, not because she is weak, but because her heart remembers things her mouth never speaks about. Sometimes she breaks down over little things, but it is not the little thing that hurt her. It is the old wound underneath it. She may need reassurance often, because somewhere in her past love felt like something that could disappear without warning. And trauma, my friend, does not always show itself in words. It shows in patterns, in silence, in overthinking, in being afraid to ask for help. Because once, depending on someone made her feel unsafe. So if you love a woman like this, do not call her difficult. Learn to see the pain behind the behavior, because understanding does not just comfort a woman. Sometimes it helps her heal. If this touched your heart, comment 100 below, and follow me for more words that heal the soul.
